utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Kolesar. If I could remind you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Mr. Vasic was in the process of still questioning you. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Kolesar.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: First of all I wanted to say the decision to continue our cross-examination today was wise, because it will shorten my cross-examination by a factor of three. I just had a look at yesterday's transcript and I have decided to drop about two-thirds of the questions that I was otherwise going to ask the witness as a result of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Splendid news, Mr. Vasic. Are you trying to suggest we should adjourn early more often?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not necessarily, Your Honour. I believe this was an exceptional situation. Thank you. Can I have the usher's assistance, please? First of all, I will be using the following document. The number in English is 2D01-0048. B/C/S is 2D01-0036.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kolesar, can you see page 1 of the statement you gave to the investigators on your screen?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in English. No, no. This is not the same document. I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this the statement you spoke about yesterday and confirmed that you gave this statement to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is page 1, "Witness," "Witness information," because that's what I see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please so that we can adjust the document in such a way that Mrs. Kolesar is looking at the B/C/S version of the document? I will require her to read a portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kolesar, can you see the B/C/S now?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In my cross-examination yesterday, I asked you about Serb patients who, after the 2nd of May, and the presence of police officers in the hospital, started to express concern because of the presence of these police officers. You answered they had no reason to worry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is on page 55 of yesterday's transcript, the 1st of November. Can the Registrar please show the following page on the screen, a page from 2D01-0049 in the English, and page 29010038 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the B/C/S page displayed on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind and read out the last two sentences from the first paragraph of your statement.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "From the clash at Borovo Selo onwards, the hospital also treated the wounded Croatian police officers, but inside the hospital they were guarded by armed police officers. At this point, the Serb patients, civilians, stopped coming to the hospital because the presence of Croatian police officers in the hospital caused them concern."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kolesar, this statement that you gave to the investigators of the Tribunal displays a discrepancy in relation to what we heard from you yesterday. Was your recollection fresher back in 1995, when you gave the statement to the investigators, or would you say that it's clearer today?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that both then and now, my recollection of this particular situation is vivid, the only question being whether I should word it differently or whether I should have the words translated from the English as we see here. The meaning, however, remains the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What you're trying to say is that the true meaning of the sentence is as expressed in the English version?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know English and I can't judge that, but the fact remains that the influx of Serb patients decreased to some extent, precisely as a result of what we talked about yesterday, namely, the presence of police officers who were guarding the wounded. Furthermore, another thing is what I spoke about yesterday. Some people weren't able to make it to the hospital. Any concerns by any Serb patients coming to the hospital were absolutely unfounded, because in all the wards throughout the hospital, including the surgery ward, there was a sufficient number of Serb doctors working, if you like, to prevent anything bad from happening to these people and to ensure that they received the best treatment possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kolesar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Registrar please now display the following page: 2D01-0051 in the English version and page 2D01-0041 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kolesar, can you see that portion on the screen in front of you? It should be page 6 of the B/C/S statement.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we also spoke about whether ZNG and MUP members came to the hospital in order to change their clothes there. I asked you about the statement you gave to the OTP. I asked you whether you in fact stated that it had been impossible to say who was actually wounded and who was merely pretending, but you said you couldn't remember and that maybe this was something that was taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is on page 76 of yesterday's transcript, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kolesar, the second sentence of the first passage, and the third sentence, can you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't following. Which specific sentences?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The second and the third in the first passage on this page.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I'm looking at. "I did not know at the time if there were Croat soldiers or defenders among the civilians inside the hospital, because I did not know who was who and there were too many people. You could not tell who was wounded and who just pretended to be wounded. The lists of wounded were given over to Dr. Bosanac, who was supposed to forward them to the International Red Cross so that they could later organise transport for the wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me now when I say that we now have the entire context for this sentence, the entire background?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, likewise. Even today, it would be difficult for me to say how, in a crowd of people, I could have known who was really wounded and who was merely pretending. There was no way I could possibly ascertain that. I just registered the fact that people were coming in. I was sure there were people who were really wounded among them, and in all likelihood there were those who were merely pretending. Whether they would be allowed to do that did not depend on me, but there was such a huge crowd, there was no way for me to tell. There were thousands of people passing through, and I was in no position to tell. If I may, I would like to provide this additional explanation. All over the world, according to conventions that you're all familiar with, a wounded person must be protected. It is perhaps not strange, given the situation that we were in, that some people should fight to attain that status, given its protected position.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Kolesar, for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours; good afternoon to my friends from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I am Borivoj Borovic, Defence counsel for Miroslav Radic. My first question: Can you please tell us about your conversation with the Tribunal investigators? In which language did you provide your statement?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking in Croatian. I signed the English version, but I believe that I was not at the time aware of these -- the discrepancies or of the style of the translation which, however, bring about such awkward situations as we have just witnessed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that your words have been clumsily translated into English?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not something that I can say, because I do not speak English. I did not go through the English version in order to be able to fully compare it to the Croatian original.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the English version of the statement was never shown to you?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with the exception of signing the statement right there on the spot, probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw Vesna Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some days ago, when we saw her off to the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who else was with her?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there, and our next witness was with us too. We came with her as far as the van, and I have no idea what happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The next witness is called what exactly?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you know that the next witness is protected?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I realised yesterday when we talked about Tomislav Hegedus and how Ms. Tuma reacted to that last name. It's not the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss the trial with Mrs. Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My statement, you mean? If I discussed that with her? We know that this is not permitted. We try to avoid that subject and we have enough to talk about any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you've been socialising these days but you have not discussed this?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you probably realised, Mrs. Bosanac has a plaster cast strapped around her leg. She was bedridden. She couldn't go to breakfast, lunch or dinner. We would bring dinner up to her room so that she could feed regularly. Every day on her way to the courtroom, I would place an elastic band on top of the plaster cast.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Kolesar. That is quite sufficient by way of an explanation. Can we now please have yes or no answers, where possible, for the next couple of questions, and then we can take it from there. First question: Was Dr. Popovic replaced, yes or no, as hospital director?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that he was replaced. I would say that there was a change in that office. I'm not aware of how that change came about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I think that you didn't quite understand my question. I asked you to give a yes or no answer. Was he replaced or no?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. My second question: Serb doctors and nurses, did they start leaving the hospital after May 1991, yes or no, bearing in mind all the explanations we heard from you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Vasic put the statement to you today, where it explicitly says that Serb patients stopped coming to the hospital after May 1991. Today, when the statement was put to you, it seemed to me that you tried to ameliorate that statement, saying that people were unable to come due to legitimate reasons.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since you require a yes or no answer, I will try to say this: What I said about people not being able to come pertained only to the surgical ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why Serb patients stopped coming after May 1991 to the surgical ward?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose because there was a number of wounded persons there. They came sporadically. There were always some wounded there, and while the wounded were there, police guarded them so this police guarding the patients was the reason why Serb patients refrained from coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean, Mrs. Kolesar, that if the Serb patients came, those who were afraid of policemen, that they would be turned back?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they would have been admitted just like all other patients. I stated quite clearly that we had a sufficient number of Serb doctors working in the surgical ward, and if patients did not trust other doctors, there were plenty -- there were certainly plenty of Serb doctors who would have been able to take good care of them in accordance with all the professional rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you know then, that they refrained from coming to the hospital as patients, people who were of Serb ethnicity? Who told you they were afraid of armed policemen? Who told you, then?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was rumoured. I can't say that I came across a patient who said, You know what, I'm not going to come because there are policemen there. No. But this was rumoured. And it is a fact that in May, we had fewer patients in the surgical ward, fewer patients of all ethnic backgrounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. So after May 1991, was the number of Serb patients in the surgical ward significantly lower or did they stop coming altogether?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of such patients was significantly lower but we did have such patients.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To make sure that we understand each other -- well, how come there were some if they stopped coming?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us be clear about this. The city of Vukovar was not blocked off at the time. There were no roadblocks and the roads leading to the hospital were fully accessible. My statement perhaps it is not clear on its face but it mostly concerns the patients, Serb patients, from villages surrounding Vukovar rather than those from the city of Vukovar. Those who lived in Vukovar were absolutely able to reach the hospital because there were no roadblocks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. But you will still agree with me that nevertheless, they stopped coming after May 1991?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them who couldn't come and didn't want to come most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I fully appreciate your attempt to stand by your statement but you have to be quite explicit and clear. My question is this: After May 1991, how many Serb patients did you have in the surgical ward? And let us conclude with this topic.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible for me to give an answer to a question phrased in those terms. I didn't go around counting Serb patients and Croatian patients, but I'm telling you firmly that we had patients of both ethnicities but fewer of them. As for the influx of new patients from Serbian villages, it was practically impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what in formal terms the National Guards Corps means?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely precisely what it means, National Guards Corps. What else could it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since the Trial Chamber and I, Witness, do not know --

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: -- including the Prosecution. Would you be so kind as to explain what it means, just in order to know it in specific terms? Is that a military formation?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me too much. I'm not a soldier. I can't know whether they belong to a particular specific military formation such as the JNA. At any rate, their name was National Guards Corps, and they were the people who defended Vukovar. I couldn't tell you exactly the formal military formation that they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a member of ZNG or National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not lined up in a group, but I saw them as wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since you did see some members, would you please explain to me and the Trial Chamber whether such persons were brought in or came in wearing a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did they have any military insignia?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say. There probably was an inscription somewhere saying National Guards Corps but I don't remember it. I wouldn't even be able to tell you whether that inscription was on their sleeve or some place else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: These formations, their members, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that they didn't go to defend the city barehanded but I didn't see any weaponry, nor did I go to their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to have weapons, if they are military, then they had to have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I think that you could have answered this in shorter terms, so let us do that in future in order not to waste time.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since yesterday, you said that one of the doctors was a member of the Main Staff of the defence of the city, would you please tell us, do you know that National Guards Corps had its main joint command in the city of Vukovar? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Matos who was the member of the staff conveyed back to us the instructions that pertained to us on transforming a civilian hospital into a hospital that would be at all times prepared for an influx of the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know who was the chief of the National Guards Corps in Vukovar or not?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I won't be able to tell you that. I have no idea who held that post during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the beginning of the conflict that you described, up until the 17th of November 1991, as head nurse, do you know how many members of the ZNG and policemen came to the hospital, were brought into the hospital or came there on their own?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the figure right now. It's been 14 years. I wouldn't be able to tell you how many precisely members of the ZNG and policemen came to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Yesterday you mentioned six soldiers and that's the only number you mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those are the people who spent sometime at the hospital and I was able to get to know them better during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did some of the doctors that you had contacts with keep record of members of military formations, ZNG, specifically their military affiliation and so on?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that information was entered into the official register book.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who secured the hospital and -- rather, was hospital secured from the outside?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were guards there. I don't know who installed them there in the hospital. I moved very little about the compound of the hospital but I know for a fact that there were guards there. What I saw were the policemen who guarded the entrance leading into the emergency room, but they were not armed. I suppose that the guards who guarded hospital buildings were armed, but I can't claim that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to tell you that director of your hospital, in her testimony here, stated that the outside security of the hospital consisted of members of the ZNG and that policemen provided security inside the building, what would you say? Would you think -- would you contradict that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't. I think that is probably right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So what is right, then? Is it what Vesna Bosanac stated, that the outside security was provided by the members of the ZNG or what you stated, that it was done by policemen?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can repeat what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the entrance into the emergency room was guarded by unarmed policemen, and just like Dr. Bosanac, I claim that the entire compound of the hospital perimeter was most likely guarded by the members of the ZNG. That makes quite a difference, because the inside area is the area where the patients were, whereas the area outside has nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mrs. Kolesar, I'm glad we clarified this. Basically, you echoed what Dr. Bosanac said, that the outside security consisted of members of the ZNG who had to be armed. They didn't guard the hospital unarmed?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why were you assigned a task from the Main Staff, as you told us, to start preparing atomic shelter as early as May 1991? Why as early as that there was a need to reactivate atomic shelter?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why? I will tell you. Atomic shelter was used to store bed-linen there. Therefore, it wasn't prepared to be used as an atomic shelter. We had not a single bed installed there and it's quite a task to organise all that. Assumption that things would unfold the way they did unfold, and occasionally we did have sporadic attacks, was absolutely logical. We had to react in this way. Every hospital has to be prepared for events that might unfold and has to ensure that they have safe environment for their patients. Now, as to those who issued that task knew exactly what was going to unfold, I wouldn't be able to tell you that, but my task was to prepare this area for patients who would potentially come there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us specifically who issued that instruction in accordance with which you acted?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was an instruction of the municipal staff, which was then conveyed to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how this was structured? Why would an instruction from municipal staff be mandatory for you? Was the workers' council duty-bound to pass a decision or was this instruction mandatory for you on its own?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was the person to whom this -- for whom this instruction was mandatory. I was the last link in the chain and I had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You told us about this auxiliary hospital that existed in Borovo Komerc, in the atomic shelter there. Did you know of any other atomic shelters in the city of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew of only one other one, in a neighbourhood called Olnica [phoen]. I didn't visit either of these two shelters, and I regret that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't see how it was prepared and under what circumstances people lived in those shelters. I only know how people lived in our shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. In August 1991, did you see two planes of the JNA which were downed, or did you hear of that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Saturday, at around noon, or in the afternoon - I'm not sure - we heard the planes flying above. Since it was possible to watch that, I did observe it. As for the moment when the plane was downed, I didn't see that but I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: One or two?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said the two planes were downed. You have to realise that all of us talked among ourselves, discussed it, therefore we heard that two planes were downed. The mere idea of two downed planes made me think that something else would ensue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Which was what?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was what happened on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that after the two JNA planes shot down, what follows next -- what followed next was a punishment?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The way I saw it, what happened the next Sunday was punishment, or at least that was my experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the exact date? You're talking about Saturday and Sunday. Which dates are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Saturday was the 24th of August and the Sunday was the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. August. Let me check what that means. Ah, August, okay. Do you know who shot down those JNA planes that were flying over the town? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard but I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone boast about that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to me. Perhaps there was someone boasting to their mates but I certainly wasn't someone that anyone like that was likely to come to in order to boast about shooting down a plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not what I was asking about. I was asking more about something that the Trial Chamber is probably unaware of. Did those planes just drop like that by themselves or were they shot down from someone firing from the ground?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there are too many planes that just fall like that. I think they must have been shot down. They must have been engaged in some form of military activity to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You seem crystal clear and perfectly convinced when you were shown your own statement yesterday. I heard that yesterday. You answered, "There were planes flying over and I saw them fall down," and now you're trying to suggest that those planes had in fact been engaging in military -- in some sort of military activity, which you have never suggested so far. I think you're trying to make a link between that and the punishment, as you said, that followed. Does that mean that they weren't actively involved, that they weren't firing over that part of town?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those two planes were not firing on the part of town where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My next question: In early October, you said that the hospital staff brought their relatives to the hospital, which was considered a safe place to be. Would I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. Their houses had been destroyed, and in comparison, the hospital could offer some degree of safety to the children.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did that have to do with the atomic shelter too?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the atomic shelter at Borovo Komerc? Do you know if there were any ill persons there?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were some ill there, as well as some of our wounded who had healed in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What did those healed wounded do there exactly?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They no longer required urgent surgical attention. They had been operated on, there was a wound that required further dressing but not necessarily in the hospital. It could be done in the shelter, so as to make room for new patients in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if records were kept in written form of persons who spent some time in the atomic shelter at Borovo Komerc?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw a single document specifying the number of patients there. Probably the doctors and the nurses who were there did keep some sort of records, but I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That means you know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Please answer yes or no: Did you ever hear that some soldiers of the JNA --

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: I would like to object to this kind of questioning from the Defence counsel. The witness should be able to make explanations when she is answering the questions. It's difficult just to have a yes and no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It depends entirely on the question, Mrs. Tuma, and I have been listening each time Mr. Borovic has put that to the witness. I nearly intervened once but the witness handled it herself. Thank you. Mr. Borovic, there are some questions that cannot be answered yes or no. The one that is most typically offered, as a joke, is, "Have you stopped beating your wife?" And if you think what yes or no signifies to that, you will realise it can't be answered yes or no. So it's true that if a witness is avoiding answering a question that is straightforward, you can certainly try to get the witness to commit to yes or no, but you will understand there are occasions when that is not possible. So please try and adjust your questions to take account of that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I believe that I've been trying very hard so far and I will continue to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point hear that at Borovo Komerc JNA soldiers years were being treated?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that some soldiers who died at Borovo Komerc were not buried but rather burned by ZNG members in order to save money?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What do you know about a neighbourhood known as Mitnica? Have you ever heard of that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about where it is?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the eastern section of Vukovar. I've lived in Vukovar for a very long time, so from my point of view this is a relatively new neighbourhood. I'm not sure about the number of inhabitants. Mostly those are private homes, a handful of shops, they had their own school and this also applies to the period before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if there were any military operations in that neighbourhood at the time?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know much about that. I do assume, however, that the people who lived in Mitnica or the ZNG, if you like, defended the area from JNA incursions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether on the 17th of November 1991, large number of members of the ZNG surrendered to the JNA at Mitnica because it was their last remaining strong hold on which occasion they also surrendered a large amount of weapons?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me this information was not linked to the 17th of November, or rather, I didn't know that at the time, but I found out later whether I saw footage and saw all of these things on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you can confirm that, though?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. I didn't know about the specific amount of weapons but I saw in this footage that each and every soldier surrendered whatever weapons they were carrying on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was that the most important stronghold of the ZNG in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not something that I can say. That would imply that I knew more about what the ZNG were doing in specific areas than I actually do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know for what reason the JNA left the hospital as the last place they entered?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that there is a theory that it was the hospital in actual fact that was the last remaining stronghold of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I definitely can't agree. I can't say what was happening outside and whether there were any strongholds, as you say, around the hospital but the hospital certainly cannot be included.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I think this is a very fair answer, so I won't press the matter. Over the last three months, September, October and November, 1991, according to your information, how many JNA soldiers were treated at the Vukovar Hospital, if you could give us a total?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't give you a total.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Four, three?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four, rather. I know Sasa, I know the other two but there were probably other wounded at the time who also required treatment. In addition to Sasa whether there were two, three or four other ones is not something I can really say right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sasa Jovic, whom you mentioned, do you know on which date he was brought to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was that in early or late October?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might as well have been early November. I don't think he stayed for over a fortnight but I can't be sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I told you that he had been brought in on the 2nd of October and that Dr. Bosanac testified that it was late in October, which of these two would you see as more -- very similar?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer would be I don't think Sasa actually stayed among us for that long. That's the best I can give you. Or perhaps time just flew by.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why was he kept in a separate ward, regardless of the conditions which you described yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't only him. There were two other JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And the reason?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said yesterday, you probably don't have a very accurate idea of what the conditions were for the wounded who lay there. What they were given was comfort.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was that the only reason, their personal comfort?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there could have been altercations between the two groups of wounded. This was a risk that was real. If you allow me to explain, when their room was shelled and destroyed, on two occasions, they had to share the same rooms with all the other wounded children and women. And the relationship turned out to be quite fair actually. They shared the same cigarettes. They shared the same difficult life that a wounded person lived in those times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us about this yesterday. Mrs. Kolesar, do you know that after the war, Sasa Jovic, soldier Sasa Jovic became mentally ill?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: How on earth would I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What would you say if I told you that Sasa Jovic alongside with the other two soldiers was being kept and guarded, rather, in the basement later in the communal rooms and that he was actually being held there as a hostage because of the international observers?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your version is something that I have never heard before, what you are suggesting now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe Sasa Jovic's injuries?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I would much sooner be able to remember the injury sustained by another soldier. I think Trifunovic was the name. He had an injured leg. He was found lying in a house. He had been lying there for two days. He had a serious infection. I remember his injuries with far greater accuracy than those of Sasa Jovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you can't say about Sasa Jovic?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm no longer able to specify his injuries, whether it was the leg, the arm or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the staff, rather, the headquarters of the hospital's Crisis Staff as its full name reads, was in touch with the JNA in those months, September October and November?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If anyone at all was in touch with them, then it must have been Dr. Bosanac but this is not something that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who else would be in a position to know this sort of thing except for Dr. Bosanac, or was she alone in a position to have that sort of communication? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Dr. Bosanac sending any faxes to anyone?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that she was dictating fax messages to her clerk. I'm not sure who eventually sent them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And to whom?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To no one. I wasn't the typist. I'm in no position to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you perhaps give us the name of that clerk?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Her name is Verica Graf.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You were the head nurse. You were moving about the hospital a great deal. You were an important person there after all. Were you ever in the room from which those faxes were being sent?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Dr. Bosanac had her own room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You never once went there?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would go there several times a day, but at the time in 1991, I don't think I even knew what a fax machine looked like or whether there was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was there one?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know. I only got to know what a fax machine looked like several years later when I first started using one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So back then, you weren't able to say, were you?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could tell a phone but not a fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Vesna Bosanac at any point in time went elsewhere, left the hospital, to give fax messages to anyone else, be it the JNA or the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she never said, "I'm going out now to send a fax."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you allow, did Vesna Bosanac ever tell you about going to the municipal staff headquarters?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe she went both to the police building and to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When specifically?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no way I could monitor her whereabouts or her actions or where she was going. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I am being cautioned to try to speak more slowly. I promise to do my best. You mentioned Bogdan Kuzmic?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: He is one of your former employees?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified that the JNA tried to prevent other people from entering the hospital who were not members of the JNA. Would I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in remembering you stating that Kuzmic and Dr. Ivankovic's son still managed to get past the security? Was this an isolated case?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are some persons that I actually saw. I can't say whether there was another entrance or other rooms where somebody else got in. This is not something that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Even on that day you were moving about the hospital, I assume, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And those were the only two persons you came across?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the hospital denotes a rather large area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about Bogdan Kuzmic? Did he treat you in a respectful manner?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was he in fact dealing out cigarettes all over the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He even boasted about being assigned the rank of colonel and -- the rank of lieutenant. He had a scar on the right side of his face. I asked him about it, boldly, in fact. He said he had been wounded, that he had been treated at the VNA in Belgrade, and then he told me who he was looking for, who the nurse was that he was looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Kolesar. Just to wrap this up, can we conclude, therefore, that no one with the exception of these two persons jeopardised the security of anyone at the hospital on that day when the two men got through?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was the JNA's duty. I believe that's why they were outside the hospital, although I didn't personally see them outside. I believe they assumed this responsibility, namely to provide security for the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we are coming to a question that you partially answered yesterday. On the 17th of November, 1991 all military operations ceased?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. In your vicinity. On the 18th, as you said, civilians continued streaming into the hospital and other persons as well because for them, the hospital represented an oasis of peace and calm?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And safety to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That's right. In your statement put to you by Mr. Vasic, on the same page that you read out from, we can see that you stated there just what you stated here. You stated previously that on the 17th and 18th, there was nothing remarkable going on. People were moving about the hospital freely. My question is: These people moved about the hospital freely, were they able to come out without any hindrance or did you perhaps prohibit them coming out?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What people do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: These civilians did not stay in the same area where the wounded were. So since I told you that the wounded were in the basement, and that this is where we worked, by that I mean our clinics and operating rooms, we were all there around the atomic shelter, the food had to be brought down there so these people went up to the floors above us, to the ground floor and all the way up as far as it was safe. I didn't go up there so I can't tell you whether they went to the surgical ward, but I did see them in the internal diseases ward. I saw them sitting there in all the rooms that were still in good shape. So yes, they were able to move around the hospital but most of them stayed where I just told you they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kolesar. My question for you is this: On the 17th, did you stay throughout the day in the hospital or did you perhaps go out?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where could I have gone then on that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the 18th? Did you go somewhere then or did you stay in the hospital the whole time?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hospital. I didn't even go out into the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were there any people in the yard?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you say "there was nothing going on in our part of the town, it was peaceful, it was safe," you stand by that statement, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no shooting around us. Yes, we could hear sporadic firing somewhere in the distance, but it didn't resemble certainly things that were happening up until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Nobody fired at the hospital, either on the 17th or the 18th?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So did you understand my question fully? On the 17th and 18th, nobody fired at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think. I don't know to what extent this is accurate, but that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you claim that it is true?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I affirm that what I'm saying is true, but I can't know whether somebody fired from a rifle somewhere in the distance. Certainly there was no shelling or bombing going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the document -- I apologise, just a minute, please. The first document, XX00-0034, Exhibit 34, admitted as Prosecution exhibit. Could the usher please take this document entitled "urgent protest" and could it be shown on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Trial Chamber see it and the OTP? Since this is Exhibit 34, it is very easy to locate the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The witness can see the B/C/S version. My question: Can the witness read out the first sentence, just below the heading "urgent protest"?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Tanks keep continuously firing at the hospital. At this moment, therefore, 600 patients in the hospital and the same number of civilians awaiting evacuation."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the date?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 18th of November 1991, at 0850.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, please, can the witness be shown the next document, XX00-0039, Exhibit 36. Could the witness please be shown the B/C/S version on her screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in so the witness can see this?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have my glasses and I can see this clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please read out the first sentence under the heading?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Artillery is active again."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is the date clear?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please re-read the date? I think you made a mistake. You didn't read out the date as is stated here.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I didn't. I apologise. 18th of November, 1991, at 1010.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 37, please? XX00-0035. B/C/S version needs to be shown to the witness, please. Can you see it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I just read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No. The next document.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it now? You have the B/C/S version don't you?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and read out the fifth line from the top? It says here, "Right now."

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Right now, there are two planes flying very lowly and attacking the city and the hospital, which has been hit with several shells in the course of the morning."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What you told us yesterday and today regarding artillery attacks on the 17th and 18th, is it true?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I as a person who was there can tell you that I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question: I don't think I have many more questions left for you. And I would like to turn now to the red cross sign. We heard from you that this sign was placed on the so-called infectious diseases ward and also on the parking lot marked with number 6, representing a part of the yard. If I were to tell you that Dr. Bosanac stated that the sign was placed on one of the auxiliary buildings and that the other sign was placed in the yard between the old and the new building, would you stand by your previous statement or would you have an additional comment?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have an additional comment and would say that there must have been then three signs because I remember the sign in the place which I marked, and I remember the sign which was placed in the then infectious diseases ward which is currently the administration building, because that roof was lower than other roofs, and it was difficult for anyone to place a sign on the highest spot. Therefore, we placed the sign on the visible spot but not necessarily the highest spot. And if there was a sign anywhere else, then it must have been the third one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see it anywhere?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that but I can't be firm about it. I believe that it did exist. There must have been more signs than I knew about, but there definitely were signs. The hospital was clearly marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. We will verify whether the signs were placed in those locations.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The part of the hospital where the infectious diseases ward was, how many storeys did it have?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The infectious diseases ward and the tuberculosis ward had just one storey.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just one storey?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And then the building where the atomic shelter was with the patients, how many storeys did it have?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Plus the roof?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plus the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the infectious diseases ward, at the time, when you say it was clearly marked, were there any patients there or not?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say. I personally don't know when the marks were placed. I don't know when it was already at the time when the hospital was subjected to attacks or perhaps that was prepared in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So do you know when it was placed?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Therefore, I can't tell you whether there were patients there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to tell us when the patients left the infectious diseases ward?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the patients of the hospital left, had to leave their wards, regular wards, on the 25th of August and had to be placed in the atomic shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The date was?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 25th of August, when the city was bombed. So from the 25th of August on, the patients did not return to any of the wards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Were these signs removed after some time?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you left on the 18th, were there any signs outside?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not even occur to me to pay attention to something like that. Perhaps there were signs, perhaps there weren't. But I was in no position to pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the witness you know, based on what you stated, Dr. Njavro, said that it was not until late October 1991 that signs were placed, albeit in other locations, not in the ones that you mentioned, and that the sign was removed very soon thereafter, would you say that it was a true statement or do you have additional comments?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comments. He probably knows better than I do what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since we saw Exhibits 48 and 49 on the ELMO, we spent one whole day watching these exhibits, you drew a very good sketch, I would kindly ask that this sketch be placed on the ELMO once again, the sketch drawn by Witness Kolesar, or perhaps you have Exhibit 49. Therefore, this is Exhibit 49. Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell us this: From the surgical ward, as you described it to us, to the Danube, what is the distance in metres?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you what it comprises and then you can make your own assessments.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: From the hospital to the Danube, what is the distance in metres?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I don't know that. There is a parking lot in front of the hospital and then comes the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it slowly. So we have a parking lot. How large is the parking lot in your view?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say. And then comes the road. And then a row of houses. And then the Danube.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. If I were to put the following question to you, across the Danube on the so-called Serbian side, if there were any tanks there, since you were present, tell us in your view from that distance across the river, through the houses, would they be able to see the roof of the infectious diseases ward?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: I don't know anything about military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, if somebody stood next to a tank and looked from the Serbian side across the river, through the houses and all those things that stood in between, because you know this quite well, better than us, because you were there, would this person be able to see the roof of the infectious diseases ward or not?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that. It would be ridiculous of me to say yes, they could or yes, they couldn't. I didn't go there. I didn't go on that side across the river. So I don't know. I also don't know whether the houses obstructed the view or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If you were in the area between the old and the new building --

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you be in the yard where you stood many times, would you be able to see from that spot the area across the Danube on the other bank of the Danube that I just described to you from that spot so there would be houses, rows of trees in between and so on?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps not from the yard but from the reception area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So not from the yard?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I stood at the end of the yard, no, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The yard marked with 6?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That one. I don't think I would be able to see from that area the bank. I would be able to see the woods and the Danube but I don't think I would be able to see further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any explanation for the fact that this sign was not placed on the main building of the hospital which had three storeys plus a roof but rather the sign was placed on the parking lot and other buildings that were not as visible?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you have to put that question to some other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, please. The answer to the last question here from the witness shows that it's only speculation from her point of view. She can't give any accurate precise answer. It's only speculations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be her answer may be, "I know nothing about it." She may know something about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the witness has already told us that she in effect knows nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we have two photographs displayed on the ELMO, please? I will then disclose the meaning behind this exercise. If the usher could please help me out. First, the colour photograph and then the next one. We can't see it on our screens. I said first the coloured one, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it now, Mrs. Kolesar?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is this what the hospital looked like back in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The same roof, the same shape, I mean?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less the same shape. But you could put it that way. It was like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you now take the pointer, please, and indicate the location of the infectious diseases ward? If we can see it in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we can't. It's to the east of what is shown in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If we could please zoom out a little bit so that we can see more of the area.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's to the east and you can't see it. You can't see it in the photograph. You can't even see a section of the old building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If we zoom out a bit more?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you just can't see it. This is just the new building of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can we move this to the left, please? Because in my photograph it can actually be seen.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the emergency building here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Was the infectious diseases ward in that area?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was a separate building behind this one, behind the emergency building. There was the infectious diseases ward and there was the TBC ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show this photograph too? This has a broader view of the scene.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think this is more use than the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you use the felt pen, please, to mark the infectious diseases ward?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am now able to tell you that this is the side of the hospital facing the Danube. To my left where you can see these cars is the emergency ward. Just behind it there is a row of buildings, and one of them is the infectious diseases ward, but you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please just mark the spot that you're indicating now?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the emergency ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Number 1, please. Put number 1 right there?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The emergency ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What's the distance to the infectious diseases ward?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please, sir. I'm talking about the -- I'm talking about the entire diameter of the emergency ward, and there is another five to ten metres behind it and then you have the infectious diseases ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to tell us the distance between the main building of the hospital and the infectious diseases ward?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to specify but I'll try to describe it and then you can see for yourself. You can figure it out. Look at this stretch between the hospital and the emergency ward and then add the same stretch to the infectious diseases ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Place number 2 where you think the second red cross sign was displaced,

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm indicating the one that I knew about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you use number 2, please, to mark that?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can we now have the black and white photograph displayed on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this may be a convenient time to break because I have a series of questions to continue with, or do you think I should press on now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's a good time, Mr. Borovic. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's a good time to break, Mr. Borovic. We'll return at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before I continue, can we go back to that first photograph, if that can please be displayed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the second photograph. Is that the one you meant, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. The first that I showed. Yes, you're right, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kolesar, if it's no trouble, could you please place the Roman numeral I down the middle?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Down the middle? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Anywhere in the middle. At the top of the building. The Roman numeral I, please. Above the building, if you can, outside the photograph. The Roman numeral I. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: By the building, you mean the main hospital building?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's precisely what I mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's also the only one we can see in this photograph, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That's right. We have analysed this photograph, and I now move that it be admitted into evidence, this photograph that is now bearing the Roman numeral I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have the other colour photograph displayed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And if Mrs. Kolesar could please make an effort and place the Roman numeral II in the same spot, down the middle, above the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that's a different angle now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We are just marking the photograph.

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that this photograph be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to explain about the numbers, I and II, but I believe the witness has already provided sufficient explanations.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 51.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to be perfectly clear and eliminate any further misunderstanding if the witness could please explain what the numbers I and II stand for in this photograph that has been marked as an exhibit, number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 1 is the building seen from the opposite river bank of the Danube, the other face or side of the hospital. I can't say exactly, but I think that is the southern side of the hospital, if you mean the first photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We have examined on the first one but now I'm talking about the Roman numeral --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that you have marked with the number 1 immediately outside what was the emergency ward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The emergency. This is the emergency ward, if that's what you're asking about. On photograph number 2, to my left, marked as number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about number 2?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is number 2, isn't it? The Roman numeral II?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have marked with an Arabic 2 another sign, another location. Am I correct in understanding it's where the red cross sign was placed, a red cross sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Arabic numeral 2, but I was told to put the Roman numeral II above the building. So I'm not sure what -- why this misunderstanding occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But you have also put an Arabic 2 in another position, and is the Arabic 2 where a red cross sign was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The red cross sign? One of the red cross signs was where the number 2 is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Arabic -- sorry, the Roman II is just above the main building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. You have been of great assistance to both the Defence team and the witness. Could we now please have the third photograph, the black and white photograph, displayed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kolesar, could you please now use this enlarged photograph -- first of all, can you put the Roman numeral III there above the building? And I'll use Arabic numerals to mark where you think the red cross signs were placed?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to have an explanation before I do that. When was this photograph taken? If someone could please specify the time that this photograph dates to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean whether this photograph is consistent with the area as you're familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: BINAZIJA KOLESAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. But if I may be allowed to ask a question, I wish to know when this photograph was taken. I have reasons for asking that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would ask the witness to please respect the procedure. I am asking the questions here. If you require any further explanations, you can no doubt obtain them from the OTP. Could you please be so kind in as far as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Borovic, that won't be good enough. Are you, Mrs. Kolesar, able to confirm that that is a photograph which shows the hospital, or part of it, as it was in 1991? Or are you not able to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's put it like this: Now that I've had a closer look, just next to the hospital building there is another smaller building, which was built later on, between 1991 and 1995. This is the administration building, as we call it. That was during the Krajina regime. The hospital was renovated. Why did I ask the question? Because the infectious diseases ward is still here, and the roof has collapsed so you can't see it. The building is still a ruin and that's what the photograph shows, but that's not how it was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to object here, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mrs. Tuma.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: As the witness is asking here, we do need to know when this photo was taking and the source from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm exploring that at the moment, Mrs. Tuma, and I'm intervening to try to speed things up in the identification of these photographs. And I've accepted the first two because the witness readily identified what was shown. She is hesitated about this so I have intervened more clearly.
